sources.name: Woori Bank Banking Guide for Foreign Customers
sources.factual_use: Passport or residence card is required; the bank may ask for employment, income, utility, or other supporting documents; branch and foreign-language service information.

sources.name: Financial Services Commission mobile foreigner residence card announcement
sources.factual_use: Registered foreign residents gained in-person banking access using the mobile foreigner residence card at an initial group of banks from March 2025.

sources.name: Seoul Foreign Portal mobile foreigner residence card issuance notice
sources.factual_use: Mobile foreigner residence cards are available to registered foreign residents aged 14 or older, with issuance routes tied to the physical card type and a phone in the resident's own name.

sources.name: Financial Services Commission deposit protection increase
sources.factual_use: Eligible deposits at KDIC-covered institutions are protected up to KRW 100 million per depositor per institution from September 1, 2025; market-performance-linked funds are not covered.

sources.name: Seoul Foreign Portal Financial Guide Book for Foreigners in Korea
sources.factual_use: Government-hosted foreigner banking guide used for process orientation and cross-checking.

sources.name: Financial Transactions Guide for Foreigners in Korea
sources.factual_use: Real-name identification, passport/residence card use, additional identity documents, account-purpose review, branch procedure, closure, and security precautions.

notes: A residence card is the strongest practical identity route, but official bank guidance also recognizes a passport; product and branch requirements vary.
A bank may request proof of employment, income, address, study, or another transaction purpose in addition to identity documents.
Mobile foreigner residence cards became usable for account opening at an initial group of banks in March 2025, with wider implementation dependent on participating institutions.
Online identity verification exists for registered foreign residents, but it does not guarantee that every bank or product supports fully remote opening.
Current 2026 deposit-protection wording must use KRW 100 million, not the older KRW 50 million text still visible on some bank pages.
The article avoids promising a universal transfer limit because account restrictions and proof needed to raise limits are bank-specific.
The article treats passport-only tourist opening as uncertain and recommends alternative payment methods rather than presenting it as guaranteed.
Community text and search suggestions were not used as factual evidence or as proof of demand.

topic_context.difference_from_existing: No live Korea Easy Guide post covers opening a resident bank account; existing payment and ATM guides address spending and cash access, not account setup.

research_method: Opened and read official Korean government, Seoul Foreign Portal, and bank guidance before writing. No search-result URL was counted as factual evidence.
